To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the new ANTs cross correlation metric performs as well as mutual information in template construction and brain extraction.
Mutual Information is a more accurate similarity metric for the construction of a high quality template than the squared intensity difference metric and is comparable to cross correlation.

1) ANTs is a powerful and versatile toolset for quantitative neuroanatomy; 2) The performance of ANTs is competitive with existing brain labeling approaches; and 3) The similarity metric has a significant impact on template construction and brain image labeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reproducible evaluation of similarity metric performance in the ANTs framework.
the impact of similarity measures on the construction of a template based on the UCLA LPBA40 dataset.
the reproducible evaluation of open source tools for the construction of optimal templates from large scale MRI brain data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutual information is the best choice for the affine component and cross correlation is the best choice of similarity metric for the deformable component in the ANTs framework.
ANTs is a state of the art tool for quantitative morphometric analyses of the human brain and that the similarity metric choice can have a significant impact on the results of the analysis.
the choice of the similarity metric is important and can affect the performance of the template based analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutual information is best for affine registration and cross correlation is best for diffeomorphic registration.

the ANTs similarity metric implementation is competitive with other state of the art tools and that mutual information affine mapping combined cross correlation diffeomorphism is the best method for brain extraction and cortical labeling.
the ANTs similarity metric implementation is a valuable and competitive addition to the neuroimaging toolkit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ANTs similarity metrics perform well and that the cross validation approach can be used for reproducible performance evaluation.

, while there are many similarities between the metrics, the best performance was obtained by using different similarity metrics for the affine and diffeomorphic components of the registration, and that the best overall performance is obtained by using the new cross correlation metric.
, for the specific problem of constructing a brain template, the choice of similarity metric has a significant impact on the resulting template and its derived labels.
